claims.text: The unmodified refractory high-entropy alloy has a homogeneous microstructure without oxide dispersoids.
Powder metallurgy or spark plasma sintering can introduce a uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion into the alloy.
The introduced Y2O3 particles will be uniformly distributed along grain boundaries and within grains.
Nanoscale Y2O3 particles act as sinks for radiation-induced defects.
Y2O3 particles attract and trap radiation-induced point defects and small defect clusters.
Trapping radiation-induced defects limits defect accumulation in the alloy.
Limiting defect accumulation reduces irradiation-induced void swelling.
Limiting defect accumulation mitigates irradiation-induced hardening.
The Y2O3 dispersion will not compromise the alloy's inherent mechanical properties.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will have approximately 20% lower defect density than the unmodified alloy after irradiation.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will have approximately 20% lower void swelling than the unmodified alloy after irradiation.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will retain tensile strength and ductility after irradiation.
The proposed benefit will hold under moderate-dose irradiation at approximately 700–900 °C.
Nonuniform nanoparticle dispersion may diminish the effectiveness of the defect-sink mechanism.
Operation outside 700–900 °C may diminish the effectiveness of the defect-sink mechanism.
Adding Y2O3 dispersoids will preserve processing feasibility for plasma-facing applications.
